Reviewed the full diff (plus the uncommitted follow-up edits in the working tree, which I cite line numbers from).

## Findings

**1. `internal/cli/transcript_store.go:108` — manifest is fully JSON-decoded on every read even when there are zero tombstones**
`excludedNow()` unconditionally calls `loadBrainManifest`, which goes through `decodeBrainManifestFile` (`internal/cli/brain_manifest_read.go:47`) — *two* full decode passes over the file (header pass, then body pass with a trailing-data probe). With no tombstones the result is provably empty: `excludedTranscriptPaths` early-returns at `internal/cli/session_privacy.go:318` on `len(stones.Excluded) == 0`, and the transaction loop in `excludedTranscriptPathsChecked` has nothing to iterate.
*Cheaper:* `if len(stones.Excluded) == 0 { return nil, stones, nil }` immediately after the tombstone load. Freshness is untouched — the tombstone file is still read fresh per read, which is the only input that can change mid-process.
*Cost:* `maxManifestBytes` is 16 MiB (`production_defaults_test.go:21`); a brain with hundreds of sessions has a manifest in the hundreds-of-KB range. Distill reads each session twice (see finding 5), so a 500-session brain pays ~1000 double-pass decodes of the whole manifest — in the overwhelmingly common no-tombstone case, 100% waste, and the dominant per-read cost.

**2. `internal/cli/transcript_store.go:117` — when tombstones do exist, the derived exclusion map is rebuilt from scratch per read**
`excludedTranscriptPathsChecked` (`session_privacy.go:481`) re-walks every manifest session *and* re-opens one privacy-transaction file per tombstone, on each read.
*Cheaper, same freshness:* `loadSessionTombstonesChecked` already computes `state.Identity` = `sha256` of the exact tombstone bytes (`session_privacy.go:219`). Memoize the derived `excluded` map keyed by that identity (plus manifest mtime+size) and recompute only on change. A purge rewrites the tombstone file, so the hash changes and the very next read still re-derives — the deliberate fresh-per-read guarantee is preserved while the O(sessions + tombstone-files) rebuild happens once.
*Cost:* 500 reads × (full manifest-session walk + one `open`/`read`/parse per tombstone). With 5 tombstones that's ~2500 redundant file opens and ~250k map lookups per command.

**3. `internal/cli/export.go:3311` (`snapshotTranscriptChunks`), reached from `transcript_store.go:306`** — every git-backed read full-scans the snapshot's entire `TreePaths` set
For each read, `readSnapshotTranscriptFromSource` iterates *all* tree paths across *all* checkpoints in the union snapshot, running `parseChunkIndex` (`HasPrefix` + `Atoi`) on each, then allocates and sorts a `chunks` slice. `snapshot.TreePaths` is immutable for the store's lifetime, so this recomputes the same answer N times.
*Cheaper:* resolve chunks once in `resolveSnapshot` while building `byRel` — one pass over `TreePaths` into `map[basePath][]string`, and store the resolved `chunks []string` in `transcriptLocation` (which already carries `sourceKey`/`sourcePath`/`sessionID`).
*Cost:* 500 sessions × ~2000 tree paths ≈ 1M string prefix comparisons + 500 slice allocations and sorts per command, replaced by a single pass. This scan was previously once-per-session-at-export; the diff moves it onto the hot read path.

**4. `internal/cli/transcript_store.go:306` → `catFileWithPolicy` (`export.go:2800`) — one `git cat-file -p` subprocess fork per transcript (per chunk)**
The read that used to be a local `open`+`read` is now a process spawn. `budgetedTranscriptRead` also materializes each chunk fully before checking the budget, so an oversized transcript still pays for the whole first chunk.
*Cheaper:* keep one `git cat-file --batch` process per store, written to over stdin (`<ref>:<path>` per line), reusing the existing `localOnly` env policy for its single spawn; same bytes, same no-egress policy, same per-blob error surface (`<oid> missing`). It also lets you enforce `maxBytes` from the announced blob size *before* reading the payload.
*Cost:* a distill/history run over 500 sessions goes from ~0 spawns to 500–1000 fork/execs at roughly 5–15 ms each — several seconds of pure process overhead, versus one spawn held open.

**5. `internal/cli/distill_cmd.go:413` (`validateDistillCanonicalInputs`) — preflight reads and discards every transcript, then the pipeline reads each one again**
The preflight calls `readCanonicalHistoryTranscript` purely for its error, discarding the bytes; `distill_cmd.go:239` and `:1600` then read the same transcripts. That was cheap when it was a second local file read; under the store it doubles findings 1–4.
*Cheaper:* either give `transcriptStore` a one-entry (or small bounded) content memo so the immediately following real read is free, or have the preflight stream via `store.Open` into `io.Discard` and stop retaining — cheapest of all, validate the tombstone gate + `byRel` location resolution without materializing bytes, which is what the preflight's "complete-or-refused" contract actually needs.
*Cost:* exactly 2× everything above for a 500-session brain: ~500 extra `git cat-file` spawns, ~500 extra full-manifest decodes, ~500 extra full-transcript allocations (each up to `maxDocumentTranscriptBytes`).

## Minor (not counted)
`transcriptStore.Close` (`transcript_store.go:91`) has no callers, and `transcriptStores` (`:78`) never evicts — the resolved `checkpointSnapshot` (all `SessionCheckpoints`, `TreePaths`, `Sources`) and any backend temp dir are pinned for the process lifetime. The comment acknowledges this for short-lived CLI commands, but the MCP surface and the memory worker are long-lived consumers of `readCanonicalHistoryTranscript`.

No startup/init-time blocking work was added — `initSnapshot` is correctly lazy and skipped entirely for bundles with materialized files, and the resolve itself (default-branch detect, branch destinations, settings read, union snapshot) happens at most once per store. No large-scope long-lived closures: `budgetedTranscriptRead` captures only `maxBytes`, `path`, and `readOne`.
